note: 'some astrologers came forward and maliciously accused the Jews' (Dan 3:8)
'wanting to learn the real reason Paul was accused by the Jews' (Acts 22:30); at Caesarea they 'bringing many serious charges that they could not prove' (Acts 25:7).

'Your accuser is Moses, in whom you have put your hope.' (John 5:45). Jesus is speaking to the Jews who sought to kill him (John 5:16-18), and the accusation is a future one before the Father rather than an episode the narrative reports.
'the men who had falsely accused Daniel were brought and thrown into the den of lions' (Dan 6:24); the charge itself is at 6:13, that Daniel shows no regard for the king or for his decree.
'When Paul had been called in, Tertullus opened the prosecution' (Acts 24:2), before Felix, having come down with Ananias the high priest.
